subject.title: TUI: Support Shift+Enter for newline (Enter to send)

question: Should OpenClaw expose a public TUI send/newline keybinding preference, or should this issue be resolved by documenting the current pi-tui defaults and fallbacks only?
rationale: Current main already has dependency-backed default multiline input, but configurable Enter/Ctrl+Enter/Shift+Enter behavior would add public TUI config, CLI, or keybinding surface, which repository policy treats as a high-bar product decision.

options.title: Document Defaults First
options.body: Add /help and docs coverage for Shift+Enter, Ctrl+J, terminal limitations, and backslash-enter fallback while keeping Enter-to-send as the only OpenClaw-owned default.

options.title: Add TUI Keybinding Config
options.body: Approve a narrow config or CLI bridge into pi-tui keybindings and require focused tests for default behavior, configured behavior, and help/docs copy.

options.title: Decline Configurable Keybindings
options.body: Keep the dependency defaults and close the configuration part by maintainer decision after docs clarify the supported composition flow.

recommendation.title: Document Defaults First
recommendation.body: Add /help and docs coverage for Shift+Enter, Ctrl+J, terminal limitations, and backslash-enter fallback while keeping Enter-to-send as the only OpenClaw-owned default.

likelyOwner.reason: The central TUI source/docs history and prior review comment point to steipete as the clearest routing owner for the docs/config-surface decision.
